verses.1: After we had escaped, we learned that the island was called Malta.
verses.2: And the native people showed us unusual kindness, for they kindled a fire and welcomed us all, because of the rain that had come and because of the cold.
verses.3: When Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened on his hand.
verses.4: When the native people saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, "No doubt this man is a murderer. Though he has escaped from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live."
verses.5: But he shook off the creature into the fire and suffered no harm.
verses.6: They were expecting him to swell up or suddenly fall down dead, but when they had waited a long time and saw nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.
verses.7: Now in the area around that place were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who received us and entertained us hospitably for three days.
verses.8: It happened that the father of Publius was lying sick with fever and dysentery. Paul went in to him, and after praying, he laid his hands on him and healed him.
verses.9: And when this had happened, the rest of the people on the island who had diseases also came and were cured.
verses.10: They also honored us with many gifts, and when we were about to sail, they put on board whatever we needed.
verses.11: After three months we set sail in a ship that had wintered at the island, an Alexandrian ship with the Twin Brothers as its figurehead.
verses.12: Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
verses.13: From there we made a circuit and arrived at Rhegium. After one day a south wind came up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,
verses.14: where we found brothers and were invited to stay with them for seven days. And so we came to Rome.
verses.15: And the brothers there, when they heard about us, came as far as the Forum of Appius and Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.
verses.16: And when we came into Rome, Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier who guarded him.
verses.17: After three days he called together the local leaders of the Jews. When they had gathered, he said to them, "Brothers, though I had done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, I was delivered as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.
verses.18: When they had examined me, they wanted to release me, because there was no charge against me deserving death.
verses.19: But when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar — not that I had any charge to bring against my own nation.
verses.20: For this reason therefore I have asked to see you and speak with you, since it is because of the hope of Israel that I am wearing this chain."
verses.21: And they said to him, "We have received no letters from Judea about you, and none of the brothers coming here has reported or spoken any evil about you.
verses.22: But we desire to hear from you what you think, for with regard to this sect we know that everywhere it is spoken against."
verses.23: When they had appointed a day for him, they came to him at his lodging in great numbers. From morning till evening he expounded the matter to them, testifying about the kingdom of God and trying to convince them about Jesus from both the law of Moses and the prophets.
verses.24: And some were convinced by what he said, but others disbelieved.
verses.25: And when they disagreed among themselves, they began to depart after Paul had made one final statement: "The Holy Spirit was right in saying to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet:
verses.26: 'Go to this people and say, You will indeed hear but never understand, and you will indeed see but never perceive.
verses.27: For this people's heart has grown dull, and with their ears they can barely hear, and their eyes they have closed, lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn, and I would heal them.'
verses.28: Therefore let it be known to you that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles; they will listen."
verses.29: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, arguing vigorously among themselves.
verses.30: He lived there two whole years in his own rented dwelling, and welcomed all who came to him,
verses.31: proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness and without hindrance.
